findings.body: The existing untrusted-attribute policy suppresses `website`, but the new `website_name` is still serialized and reveals the website host (and, for matching domains, its path).
findings.failure_mode: A field intentionally hidden from restricted viewers remains inferable through its derived display value.
findings.impact: The existing untrusted-attribute policy suppresses `website`, but the new `website_name` is still serialized and reveals the website host (and, for matching domains, its path).
findings.root_cause: The new derived attribute was added to the serializer without the authorization predicate used for the source `website` field.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same restriction as `website` to `website_name`, for example add it to `untrusted_attributes` or implement `include_website_name?` that returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true; add an anonymous-TL0 serialization test with a populated website.
findings.title: Do not expose a derived website field when website is restricted
findings.trigger: An anonymous visitor views a TL0 user's profile while `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true and that user has a website configured.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `:website_name` at line 43 without adding it to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) which includes `:website`. The `include_website_name` method (line 153) only checks `website.present?` and does not check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. This allows anonymous viewers to see `website_name` for TL0 users even when `website` is hidden.

findings.body: ActiveModel serializer conditional hooks use `include_<attribute>?`; this method is not invoked, so `website_name` is emitted as a null attribute instead of being omitted as the attempted predicate indicates.
findings.failure_mode: The serializer ignores the intended optional-attribute condition and changes response shape for profiles with no website.
findings.impact: ActiveModel serializer conditional hooks use `include_<attribute>?`; this method is not invoked, so `website_name` is emitted as a null attribute instead of being omitted as the attempted predicate indicates.
findings.root_cause: The newly added inclusion hook omits the required trailing question mark.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and retain the presence check (while also applying the website visibility restriction).
findings.title: Use the serializer's conditional predicate naming convention
findings.trigger: Any user profile without a website is serialized.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 153 shows `def include_website_name` without trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer conditional inclusion requires `include_<attr>?` naming convention. The method will not be invoked as a predicate, so `website_name` will always be serialized (as null when website is absent) rather than conditionally omitted.

raw_findings.body: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so the serializer returns only `EXAMPLE.com` rather than the required complete `EXAMPLE.com/user` path for a same-domain website.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Equivalent same-domain URLs are classified as external websites and lose their displayed path.
raw_findings.impact: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so the serializer returns only `EXAMPLE.com` rather than the required complete `EXAMPLE.com/user` path for a same-domain website.
raw_findings.root_cause: Raw URI host and configured hostname strings are compared without hostname normalization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize both parsed website and instance hostnames (at least lowercase, and preferably remove a trailing DNS dot) before all equality and suffix comparisons; add a mixed-case hostname spec.
raw_findings.title: Normalize hostnames before deciding that a website is on this instance
raw_findings.trigger: The instance hostname is `example.com` and a user saves an equivalent, valid URL with a differently cased host, such as `http://EXAMPLE.com/user`.

finding.title: Normalize hostnames before deciding that a website is on this instance
finding.trigger: The instance hostname is `example.com` and a user saves an equivalent, valid URL with a differently cased host, such as `http://EXAMPLE.com/user`.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 141 shows `if website_host == discourse_host` using direct string comparison. Ruby's `URI#host` returns the host as-is without case normalization. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so `EXAMPLE.com` vs `example.com` would fail the equality check, causing the path to be omitted for same-domain URLs with different casing.
